Let me start with an apology to all of you if I seem out of it. I am actually in the ICU with my dad doing this while he is sleeping. So if my posts seem to be off, or if I am asking a weird question just know that my mind is in two places. I attached a chart below that LP had above. My question has to do with the FTR that the yellow arrow is pointing to. I am noticing that I think we have an FTR drawn two different ways. In a past post Dr. Swing would have used the engulf of the purple line that I drew and the second purple arrow would have been the FTR. It looks like LP used an engulf of an old swing low and the failed move up was the FTR. So I was just drawing everyones attention to this to see if there is something I am missing, or perhaps if either is acceptable. It might even be me trying to get everything to a fine point. I just wanted to make sure we are all on the same page. Lets see what Dr. Swing has to say and we can all work on this together.

Thanks,

Hotochin, I hope all goes well for your dad, and I guess it's good to have this forum as a distraction while in ICU.

I see the market as having zones within zones within zones, and so FTRs can be located in many areas on a chart. On this M5 chart there is so much CP on show that I am just not interested until price moves away from there, and hence why I posted the M15 chart to get a clearer view of where the edges of price can be found.

I really need price patterns to scream at me, and if I have to look closely at a chart to determine what is happening, then I need to move up a tf or two or move to a different pair altogether. My viewing of a chart is usually done on the H4 tf or higher to determine my areas of interest, and only then do I move to the LTFs to pin point my entry. I see no value in wrecking my head

trying to decipher what is happening solely on an M5

chart. As rcmacf stated, the simpler the better.

Hotochin wrote: Your chart above looks good Dr. Swing. I have to say that when I apply what you have mentioned to the charts it seems to make sense. Your charts are so clear. I think the problem for me is that when I read other posts on this forum I can't make out how they are drawing their zones. Its almost like they are doing something completely different. Just a question, in the classroom IF had mentioned CP and to look for the engulf of the CP to find the zone. Have you made any sense of this comment? I am wondering if he just means the general engulf of a consolidated zone.

Thanks,

Yes H, if you follow everyone's interpretation it can lead to confusion. I originally followed the postings that made things clear for me, and now I just work through the charts on the principles learned, to develop my own interpretation.

My understanding is that IF looks for CP on the HTF, the BO from the CP and the level at which price flags and fails to return to the CP. This becomes the FTR and the edge of the PAZ. He then waits for price to return to the FTR and uses the M1 chart to locate his entry within the FTR. But this is just my interpretation from his postings:).

بله H، اگر تفسیر همه را دنبال کنی می‌تواند به سردرگمی منجر شود. من ابتدا پست‌هایی را دنبال کردم که چیزها را برایم روشن می‌کردند، و حالا فقط چارت‌ها را بر اساس اصول یادگرفته کار می‌کنم تا تفسیر خودم را بسازم.

You guys are great!

Thanks for all of your opinions.

I know I made more out of that little chart than needed, but I like trying to understand things when they don't make sense to me. I totally agree with keeping things simple. just have a tendency to get stuck in the details and not look at the overall picture. This was just a study of price to me. Just like Drswing said, if we wanted to we could go into each of my little PAZs and find many tiny s/r levels and their ftrs. But that just isn't practical when comes down to making money, its too detailed and would create too much doubt and emotions would take over. If price doesn't make sense, then stay out until it does. The things we look for should find you, not the other way around. Sorry if anyone feels a little more confused than they used to be.

Thanks again for all the discussion.

posts.t:
You just have to know that a compression itself is a PAZ (Price Action Zone)

Then you have to look where its decision was made to break it (e.g by liq spike) - you can also refer to it as decision point.

Look at your chart at the first liq spike from that cp. We tested it one time after the break, but then created a nice bullish momentum bar which broke this "FTR"
posts.fa:
فقط باید بدانی که خود کامپرشن یک PAZ است (ناحیهٔ پرایس اکشن)

بعد باید ببینی تصمیم شکستنش کجا گرفته شد (مثلاً با اسپایک لیکوییدیتی) — می‌توانی به آن نقطهٔ تصمیم هم بگویی.

به چارتت در اولین اسپایک لیکوییدیتی از آن CP نگاه کن. یک بار بعد از شکست تستش کردیم، اما بعد یک کندل مومنتوم صعودی خوب ساخت که این «FTR» را شکست
